## Findings
- claim-1: The 2011 paper treats minimality of the two Theorem 5.4 generating sets as a conjecture, while it separately presents \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) as a stronger suspected statement. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The 2024 candidate’s supplied abstract states only: “We prove the minimality conjecture.” [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- claim-3: A free integral indecomposables statement \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\), with the specified \(N\) generators mapping to a basis, implies their minimality; the converse does not establish torsion-freeness or identify \(J/\Lambda_+J\) as \(\mathbb Z^N\).
- claim-4: No bounded 2024 full-text passage with stable theorem locator, hypotheses, or coefficient-ring statement was supplied; therefore applicability of the 2024 theorem to the present integral \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is unverified.
## Strategy
**Target not established.** No bounded 2024 full-text passage with stable locator is supplied, so the required source-refresh certificate cannot be completed.

Independently, free integral indecomposables imply minimality (given an \(N\)-element generating family), but not conversely. Indeed, for
\[
A=\mathbb Z[x],\qquad J=(2x,x^2),
\]
the pair \((2x,x^2)\) is irredundant, while
\[
J/A_+J=J/(2x^2,x^3)\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2,
\]
not \(\mathbb Z^2\). Thus minimality does not imply torsion-freeness or a specified integral basis of indecomposables.

## Gaps
Missing are 2024 theorem-level full text: exact statement, hypotheses, coefficient ring, definitions matching \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), \(a,b\), and the two source families. Hence neither applicability of the 2024 minimality theorem nor any stronger statement
\[
J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}
\]
is source-established here.

## Next
A valid continuation requires supplied versioned 2024 full-text excerpts with stable theorem/definition locators; only then can minimality and integral indecomposables conclusions be compared line-by-line.
